Position Summary...

The Site Experience Intern will support work that helps make shopping on Walmart’s digital platforms simpler, more seamless and more inspiring for customers. In this role, you’ll partner with teams across Site Experience and the broader business to explore opportunities, analyze information and contribute to initiatives that improve the customer experience on Walmart’s website and app.

This is an opportunity to learn how a large-scale eCommerce organization operates, build relationships across teams and apply your skills to business challenges. Specific projects and responsibilities will vary based on business needs and your interests and skills.

The Internship: Held over an 11-week period during the summer of 2027 for students in their penultimate year of college. What you'll do...

About the Team

Site Experience owns how the digital shopping experience comes together for Walmart customers. Our mission is to connect more people to the right items and experiences in the moments that matter most.

Our teams work together across the shopping journey – from helping customers discover products through search, personalization, content and navigation to making it easier to evaluate items and complete a purchase. We also explore new ways to shop and bring innovative experiences to life, while aligning our strategy and operations around shared customer and business outcomes.

Across Site Experience, we collaborate with partners in product, technology, design and the broader business to continuously improve today’s experiences and create what’s next.

What You’ll Do

- Support a project or initiative that improves the digital shopping experience or how our teams operate.

- Gather and analyze information to identify trends, opportunities and potential solutions.

- Learn about customer needs and business priorities, and bring those perspectives into your work.

- Partner with associates across teams to develop ideas, solve problems and move work forward.

- Explore and apply emerging technologies, including agentic AI tools and vibe coding, to support research, generate ideas, build solutions or improve ways of working.

- Organize project information, track progress and communicate updates to stakeholders.

- Create clear presentations, summaries or other materials to share insights and recommendations.

- Explore opportunities to improve processes, tools or ways of working.

- Participate in team meetings, learning opportunities and the broader Walmart internship experience.

What You’ll Bring

- Curiosity about eCommerce, digital experiences and how customers shop.

- A customer-focused mindset and interest in solving problems.

- Strong analytical skills and comfort gathering, interpreting and drawing insights from information.

- Curiosity about AI and emerging technologies, including an interest in using agentic AI tools and natural-language prompts to explore problems and build solutions.

- Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to share ideas and ask thoughtful questions.

- A collaborative approach and willingness to build relationships with people across teams.

- An organized, proactive approach to managing your work and following through on commitments.

- Adaptability and a willingness to learn in a changing environment.

- Familiarity with common productivity tools, such as spreadsheets and presentation software.

Office Environment: Corporate, in-person internship

Desired Majors: General Business, Retail/Buying, Merchandising, Economics, Data Analytics, Information Systems, Marketing, Strategy, Entrepreneurship

RoboForce is an AI robotics company developing Physical AI–powered Robo-Labor for dull, dirty, and dangerous work. The company’s robots are engineered for demanding industrial environments, with a focus on real-world deployment and scalability.

We are seeking a Machine Learning Engineer Intern to join us in developing advanced AI capabilities for robotics. The internship starts from November 2026 for 3-6 months. As part of our team, you will help build the foundational AI ecosystem, spanning data collection, labeling, training, evaluation, and deployment.

You will collaborate closely with a team of world-class AI engineers and gain hands-on experience solving real-world challenges at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics.

- Train and improve robot foundation models, including vision-language-action (VLA) models and world-action models, for precise, contact-rich manipulation in industrial settings.

- Explore new modalities and methods, including tactile and force-torque sensing, reinforcement learning, and simulation, to advance model capabilities.

- Build data pipelines for robot learning, including data collection, curation, labeling, and dataset quality assurance.

- Design and run evaluations in simulation and on real robots to measure and improve model performance.

- Deploy models on robots and optimize them for real-time onboard inference.

- Work closely with robotics, hardware, and product teams to bring models from research to production.

Requirements

- Currently pursuing an advanced degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field, with a graduation date in 2026 or 2027.

- Proficiency in multimodal models, modern machine learning architectures (e.g., transformers and diffusion models), and reinforcement learning.

- Proficiency in deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.

- Requires 5 days/week in-office collaboration with the teams.

Bonus Qualifications

- Exposure to robot learning using tactile and/or vision-based sensors.

- Expertise in object pose estimation, bimanual manipulation, and synthetic data.

- 3–6 months, full-time

Compensation:

- $5,000 - $6,500 monthly salary

Atalanta is a mathematical AI company bringing provably correct decision-making to the world’s most important missions.

Our flagship product, Argo, is the first platform in a new category called software understanding. Argo combines AI, formal methods, and digital engineering to help organizations design, implement, and deploy complex software-controlled systems with mathematical assurance at mission speed.

Backed by leading investors, Atalanta works with customers building and deploying mission-critical systems across energy, space, and defense. Our goal is to help engineers and mission owners move faster while maintaining the highest possible level of assurance, ultimately saving time, money, and lives.

To learn more, here are some pieces written by Atalanta’s founders that offer deeper context on the ideas behind the company’s mission:

- Back to the Building Blocks

- The AI Arms Race Will Be Won On Mathematical Proof

/ HOW WE WORK

Atalanta takes its name from the mythological Greek heroine, a swift and fearless competitor who defied expectations and joined the Argonauts on a mission few thought possible. Her spirit of speed, discipline, and resilience shapes how we work.

We’re building a team of modern-day Argonauts: exceptional engineers, mathematicians, designers, and strategists committed to solving the hardest, highest-stakes problems in the world. We move fast, but we do so with discipline and logic. We think from first principles and execute with autonomy and accountability.

You may be a good fit for Atalanta if you are insatiably curious in the face of discomfort, are a coalition builder who sees progress as a positive-sum game, and believe that the alchemy of interdisciplinary expertise can solve seemingly impossible problems.

/ ENGINEERING AT ATALANTA

Software understanding is about building systems that perform reliably in real-world missions where failure has consequences. It requires proving that those systems behave correctly in ways that enable reliable decision-making under real-world conditions. This cannot be achieved through traditional software development alone, nor through formal methods in isolation. Atalanta’s engineering function is built on a deliberate combination of forward-deployed engineers, formal methods engineers, and software engineers, each working directly against real mission problems and real user needs: deploying into operational environments, establishing provable guarantees, and building scalable systems. This work is defined by deep mission and customer obsession, where real-world use drives what gets built and which problems matter. Engineers take a product-first approach, translating these insights into systems that can be deployed quickly across constrained and high-stakes environments. These roles operate in close coordination, ensuring that Argo continuously evolves through use in the field. Success means solving problems that were previously considered impossible, and turning them into capabilities that can be productized at scale.

As a Forward Deployed Engineering Intern at Atalanta you will work alongside our forward deployed engineers to bring Argo into customer environments and help users apply formal methods to their own systems.
